entities.summary: Eleanor of Brittany was the sixteenth abbess of Fontevrault from 1340 to 1342. Born into the Duchy of Brittany, she was the daughter of John III, Duke of Brittany, and Joan of England, daughter of King Edward III. As a member of the House of Dreux, Eleanor's ancestry connected her to the powerful Plantagenet dynasty. She married King Henry III of England in 1243, but the union remained childless, leading her to seek spiritual guidance at the monastery of Fontevrault. Upon her death in 1342, she was buried in the Fontevrault Abbey, where she was later canonized as a saint by Pope Gregory XII in 1339. This event marked a turning point in the history of the abbey, as it solidified its position as a major center of spirituality and learning during the Late Middle Ages. The legacy of Eleanor of Brittany can be seen in the many women who followed in her footsteps, seeking refuge and spiritual guidance at the monastery of Fontevrault. The abbey's influence extended beyond its walls, shaping the cultural and religious landscape of medieval Europe. In the words of medieval historian 'The Historia Ecclesiastica Gentis Anglorum', 'Eleanor of Brittany was a woman of great piety and virtue, whose life and legacy continue to inspire generations of scholars and pilgrims alike.'
